Title: ​Asthma on the rise in Pakistan
NewsSummary: "Asthma is on the rise in Pakistan," revealed Dr. Javaid A. Khan, Associate Professor & Consultant Chest Physician at the Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH). He was giving a presentation on "Asthma - A Global Health Problem."
NewsContent:
​"Asthma is on the rise in Pakistan," revealed Dr. Javaid A. Khan, Associate Professor & Consultant Chest Physician at the Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH). He was giving a presentation on "Asthma - A Global Health Problem" at 'Signs, Symptoms and Care' a monthly health awareness programme held on April 29, 2000, on the occasion of the forthcoming Asthma Day.

Dr Khan informed that, "there are over 150 million people in the world suffering from asthma. In Pakistan 10% of children and 5% of adults are suffering from this disease. This year, the theme of World Asthma Day is 'let every person breathe' emphasize the need for the asthma sufferer to have access to timely diagnosis, receive appropriate treatment, and learn how to manage their asthma with the help of health professionals." He further added that, "national as well as international guidelines for asthma management is available, but is not being implemented in Pakistan."

"In Pakistan there are a lot of misconceptions particularly in the relation of diet and asthma. Dietary restrictions are of no help to asthma sufferers. The patient should eat a normal diet like any other normal person," stressed Dr S. Ijlal babar, Consultant Chest Physician at AKUH.

Dr S. Fayyaz Hussain, Head of Pulmonary Section at AKUH, stated that, "the reason for worldwide rise in asthma is still not fully understood but in a developing country, like Pakistan, environmental pollution, rising prevalence of smoking and increased indoor and outdoor exposures to various allergens are some of the factors that are responsible for this increase."

Talking about the treatment of asthma, Dr Raana Haqqee, Assistant Professor at AKUH said that, "inhalers are safe and very effective for the relief of asthma symptoms provided they are used with correct technique." She added that anti-asthma medications are safe in pregnancy.

Dr Khan concluded by saying that, "If asthma is properly diagnosed and treated the vast majority of such patients should be able to live a normal life. However, if asthma is not properly treated then it will lead to a significant morbidity and mortality. There is a tremendous need for educating both doctors and patients about this rising epidemic in Pakistan." ​
